title: Shape a multi-screen web app in the Studio and promote the approved design
goal: You want a small two-screen web app — a tip calculator with a separate settings screen is exactly the size you mean, and you would be annoyed if anyone padded it out with more screens — and you want a say in how it looks before anyone builds it. You are deliberately economical: one batch of prototypes, one pointed reaction, approve, hand it over. Get prototypes on screen, react to ONE thing the way you would react to a colleague's draft, see your reaction taken up, approve what you end up with, and hand that to the builders. The feedback loop is the part you actually care about: you will not approve or hand anything over until you have typed one comment on a prototype, read what it will tell the designer before sending it, sent it, and watched the design change in response — if you cannot manage that, walking away without promoting anything is the honest outcome.
steps: Ask for the small two-screen app and watch the prototypes arrive on the canvas as they are made
Find the critique of what was generated without going into settings to switch anything on
Point at something on a prototype and say what you want changed about it
See exactly what your comment will tell the designer before anything is sent
Apply it, and see the design change in response
Approve the design you have arrived at
Promote that approved design into work, and read the tasks, criteria, journeys and estimate before confirming
